overview:
Joy P. Deupree, PhD, MSN, CRNP, WHNP-BC is a Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Executive Nurse Fellow (2014-2017) and served as an appointed member to the Alabama Governor's Health Care Improvement Task Force (2015-2018). While on the AGHCITF she developed the infrastructure for the Alabama Health Literacy Initiative and chaired it until 2019 when she relocated to the University of South Carolina College of Nursing at the University of South Carolina in Columbia, South Carolina.  While at U of SC, she was a professor and served as Associate Dean for Office of Practice and Innovation, Partnerships and Policy and was Co-Chair of the Center for Nursing Leadership for the state of SC located and housed at the College of Nursing. In May, 2023, she returned the UAB School of Nursing and is working with Dean Maria Shirey to develop new programs for the School of Nursing.  She is faculty in the DNP Policy and Politics Course and the course manger for the PhD Policy Course taught in the SON. Since returning to UAB, she has been named as a Co-Lead for the AARP and RWJF Future of Nursing State Action Coalition in Alabama (AL-HAC) in association with the Sylacauga Alliance for Family Enhancement (SAFE) in Sylacauga, Alabama.  SAFE serves the poor and underserved surrounding communities and has a robust research agenda to improve the Social Determinants of Health. 

She has been actively involved in policy change for nurse practitioners in the state of Alabama since 1996 when as a member of the Legislative Committee for the Alabama State Nurses Association she was among those who worked on passage of legislation that developed the infrastructure for NPs to prescribe legend drugs and have a collaborative practice. In 2001, she was appointed by the Governor of Alabama to serve on the Alabama Board of Nursing in one of two dedicated APRN seats; she served in that role for two terms. In 2006 after leaving service to the Alabama Board of Nursing, seeing the need for NPs to have a strong voice and advocate for policy change to remove barriers to practice, she and five other NP colleagues in Alabama founded the Nurse Practitioner Alliance of Alabama (NPAA). In 2012, she was elected president of NPAA and in 2012-2013, as president of NPAA she championed efforts to pass legislation allowing APRNs to prescribe controlled substances (Schedules II-V).  From 2014-2019, Dr. Deupree served as the senior adviser for policy for NPAA, which represents the interests of more than 7,000 NPs in Alabama. Her advocacy work for legislative change to reduce barriers for APRNs in Alabama and her advocacy efforts for health literacy initiatives in part led to her being chosen as one of 20 nurses in America for the highly competitive Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Executive Nurse Fellows Program (2014-2017). From 2015-2018, she was an appointed member of the Alabama Governor's Health Care Task Force where she led efforts to establish the Alabama Health Literacy Initiative now housed at UAB School of Nursing and recognized by the Centers of Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) as an official state health literacy initiative. 

In 2018 as senior policy adviser for the NPAA she led coordinated efforts for passage of HB 429 in the Alabama Legislature to allow NPs and CNMs the ability to sign 22 additional documents that previously only physicians could sign causing great disparities due to backlog of approval for these forms many times delaying payment by insurance and treatment for care. Dr, Deupree has authored and co-authored numerous publications and has been a keynote and breakout speaker at many  state, national and international conferences. 

Dr. Deupree has been recognized for her leadership in research, teaching, policy, and health literacy at the national, state and local level.  Nationally, she was named as an Ambassador for the Friends of the National Institutes for Nursing Research (NINR) in 2022 and regularly corresponds, visits, and communicates with congressional leaders regarding the need for increased funding for research at the NINR and in 2023 she was inducted into the American Academy of Nursing. State recognition awards she has received for her advancement of policy and efforts to bring awareness to health literacy and other disparities associated with the social determinents of health include inducation into the Alabama Nursing Hall of Fame (2023), the Alabama Healthcare Hall of Fame2024, the American Assoication of Nurse Practitioners State Advocacy Award (2024) and the "Power of One" Award from NPAA (2014) for her policy leadership to pass legislation for controlled substances II-V and other legislative successes and rule changes. In 2021, she was named a Visionary Leader by UAB School of Nursing.

With more than 30 years as a policy advocate at the state and national level, she regularly addresses nursing groups in an effort to mentor other nurses using experiential opportunities that prepares them for advocacy at the state and national level.
